title: TNF as a granuloma-maintenance node
dek: Wikipedia's tumor necrosis factor page is the cytokine. Anti-TNF reactivation logic stays on tb-tnf-cd4.
story: TNF on Wikipedia is a trimeric cytokine with jobs in inflammation, cachexia (the old name cachectin), and granuloma maintenance. TB programmes care because blocking it for rheumatoid arthritis and similar diseases reopens mycobacterial control.
The clinic plate tb-tnf-cd4 already walks screening and TPT around anti-TNF. This card is the molecule in the encyclopedia graph, sitting next to IFN-γ and the granuloma class.
TNF is not 'the TB toxin' and not an antibiotic. Cachexia in advanced TB is multifactorial; do not reduce it to one Wikipedia lead.
deep: Infliximab, adalimumab, etanercept are different agents with different TB reactivation stories; that nuance is clinic, not this glossary.
Soluble receptor versus monoclonal antibody is a pharmacology fork the encyclopedia will mention; programmes still follow WHO/CDC around testing and TPT.
TNF from macrophages and T cells is why HIV (CD4 loss) and anti-TNF rhyme.
Do not prescribe anti-TNF reversal from this card.

visual.caption: TNF as a maintenance signal on the granuloma. Pharmacologic blockade is the clinical hazard handed to tb-tnf-cd4.
